status: Single exploratory screen specified after seeing edit and ordinal performance, eligibility counts and the first order-reversal example. Scores of the new rule have not been computed. Same records, not independent confirmation.
hypothesis: The identities of other parts manipulated around a repeated fine action contain occurrence-specific evidence when the chronological order of two operations differs between people.
rule: For every event in each complete fine-action transcript, count nouns in the previous eight and next eight events, excluding all occurrences of the anchor's own noun. Treat each of the sixteen positions equally. Use cosine similarity between two occurrence count vectors of the same fine action, zero if either vector is empty. Ties share credit, computed via exact squared cosine fractions. All target instances remain eligible, without coarse labels. Apply the rule once, without changing windows, vocabulary, weights or input after seeing outcomes.
decisions: Report complete paired scores on the same 60 directed swaps, reversed and same-order separately, and single-cue ranking on the original 212 items. Report distinct toy count where both required target events are uniquely identified on a reversed transfer. Advance this simple rule beyond the current feasibility panel only if it yields unique dual-cue successes on reversed cases from at least two toys and exceeds the existing fixed edit matcher on all 212 single-cue items. Other results motivate new questions but no optimization on this panel. Artificially substituting uniform-choice scores supplies an exact chance comparator. Target action labels and future context are available; this is annotation-based retrospective localization.
